_doc: Items still failing after their ONE repair (owner rule 19 Nov): kept out of points.json; the clauses stay plain checklist items until the owner decides.

items.question: Was the control strategy for all manufacturing stages developed using QRM principles to minimise variability and the chance of contamination and cross-contamination?
items.verify: Verify that QRM principles are used to develop the control strategy across all stages of manufacture so as to minimise variability and reduce the opportunity for contamination and cross-contamination.

evidence.what: control strategy
QRM records behind the control strategy

items.why: no_less: The verify and question drop the scope 'for this class of materials' (biological active substances and finished products) and the point that QRM principles are 'particularly important' for them, so the duty reads as applying to any manufacture.

clauses.text: As a result, QRM principles are particularly important for this class of materials and shall be used to develop the control strategy across all stages of manufacture so as to minimise variability and reduce the opportunity for contamination and cross-contamination.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Do manufacturing records show that products are made to be fit for use, in line with their marketing or clinical trial authorisation, and without risk to patients from poor safety, quality or efficacy?
items.verify: Verify that the holder of the Manufacturing Authorisation manufactures medicinal products so as to ensure that they are fit for their intended use, comply with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation or Clinical Trial Authorisation, as appropriate, and do not place patients at risk due to inadequate safety, quality or efficacy.

evidence.what: records showing manufacture complies with the Marketing Authorisation or Clinical Trial Authorisation requirements
Marketing Authorisation or Clinical Trial Authorisation requirements held on site

items.why: no_more: The evidence wording 'held on site' adds a location requirement for the authorisation documents that the unit does not state.

clauses.ref: EU GMP Part I, Chapter 1, Principle
clauses.text: The holder of a Manufacturing Authorisation must manufacture medicinal products so as to ensure that they are fit for their intended use, comply with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation or Clinical Trial Authorisation, as appropriate and do not place patients at risk due to inadequate safety, quality or efficacy.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Are management review results and actions written down, shared in good time and raised to senior management where needed (recommended)?
items.verify: Verify that the results of the management review and actions are documented and communicated in a timely and effective way, including escalation of appropriate issues to senior management (recommended).

evidence.what: management review results and actions
records showing communication and escalation of the results

items.why: no_more: The lead-in says the outcome 'can include' item (h), which is only a possibility, but the point turns it into a recommendation by marking it '(recommended)'.

clauses.text: (h) Documentation and timely and effective communication of the results of the management review and actions, including escalation of appropriate issues to senior management.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Does the PQR contain the relevant information that the MAH itself holds (recommended)?

MAH-held information relevant to the PQR

items.why: no_more: The unit only says the MAH "can ensure" its information is included, as one way it "may add value"; marking this "(recommended)" turns an option into a recommendation.

clauses.ref: EMA reflection paper GMP and MAHs, 5.4 ¶9
clauses.text: • The MAH can ensure that information that it holds which is relevant to the PQR is actually included in the PQR.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.why: code: A8 question drops the qualifier '\bminimi[sz]'

items.question: For investigational ATMPs, do release records show that the QP's checks match the development stage, including that the manufacturer's quality specifications are met for a device still under investigation (recommended)?
items.verify: Verify that, in the case of investigational ATMPs, the checks reflect that the amount of relevant information available depends on the stage of development (e.g. where medical devices used in an investigational combined ATMP are in an investigational phase as well, the QP ensures that the quality specifications set by the manufacturer are respected) (recommended).

evidence.what: batch release records of investigational ATMPs
quality specifications set by the manufacturer

items.why: no_more: The point marks the QP's role "to ensure that the quality specifications set by the manufacturer are respected" as "(recommended)". The unit states this as the QP's role, not a should-recommendation. The question also turns the descriptive "amount of relevant information available will depend on the stage of development" into a duty that "the QP's checks match the development stage".

clauses.text: 11.29. In the case of investigational ATMPs, the amount of relevant information available will depend on the stage of development (e.g. medical devices used in an investigational combined ATMP may be in an investigational phase as well and, in such cases, the role of the QP is to ensure that the quality specifications set by the manufacturer are respected).

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

evidence.what: qualified person's batch assessment records

items.why: no_more: The lead-in only permits ('may include as appropriate'), but the point turns this into a recommendation: 'includes batch records ... (recommended)'.

clauses.text: i. Batch records, including control reports, in-process test reports and release reports demonstrating compliance with the product specification file, the order, protocol and randomisation code.

documents certifying the manufacturer's authorisation

items.question: Do release records show that products meet their approved specifications, with release normally based on the full set of tests set in the authorisation?
items.verify: Verify that medicinal products comply with their approved specifications. Subject to compliance with GMP, they can normally be released to market by performing a complete set of tests on active substances and/or finished products as defined in the relevant marketing authorization or clinical trial authorization.

evidence.what: approved specifications
test results and batch release records

items.why: no_more: The question's 'with release normally based on the full set of tests set in the authorisation' turns the unit's permission ('can normally be released ... by performing a complete set of tests') into a condition that release records must show.

items.question: Does the MAH itself follow each of these recall requirements and have systems in place for its recall activities?
items.verify: Verify that each of these recall requirements is applied to the MAH, given the MAH's role in recall decision making, coordination and management, and that the MAH has systems in place to deal with these activities.

evidence.what: MAH systems for recall decision making, coordination and management
records showing the MAH applies the recall requirements

items.why: answerable: The question and verify say "each of these recall requirements" without naming them. These are the ¶10 duties: periodic effectiveness evaluation, covering office and out-of-office hours, considering mock recalls, and documented and justified evaluations. An auditor therefore cannot tell from the point what to check for a YES/NO.

clauses.ref: EMA reflection paper GMP and MAHs, 5.5 ¶11
clauses.text: Each of these requirements is applicable to the MAH, given the MAH’s role in recall decision making, coordination and management, and it is important that the MAH has systems in place to deal with these activities.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Do the heads of production and quality control, and of quality assurance where there is one, share the listed quality system responsibilities (recommended)?
items.verify: Verify that the person responsible for production, the person responsible for quality control and, where applicable, the person responsible for quality assurance share some responsibilities regarding the design and implementation of the pharmaceutical quality system, in particular concerning training, documentation obligations, process validation, validation of the transport conditions and of the reconstitution process (where applicable), control of the manufacturing environment, control of outsourced activities, and quality investigations (recommended).

evidence.what: documents or records showing the responsibilities of these persons

items.why: no_more: The unit states as fact that these persons 'share some responsibilities', with no 'should'; marking the question and verify '(recommended)' weakens it to a recommendation.

clauses.text: The person responsible for production, the person responsible for quality control, and - where applicable- the person responsible for quality assurance, share some responsibilities regarding the design and implementation of the pharmaceutical quality system and in particular concerning training, documentation obligations, process validation, validation of the transport conditions and of the reconstitution process (where applicable), control of the manufacturing environment, control of outsourced activities, and quality investigations.

items.question: Where products are made in a closed system or an isolator, is the surrounding clean area of the grade stated as acceptable (recommended)?
items.verify: Where production takes place in a closed system, in an isolator, or positive pressure isolators, verify that the background clean area is of grade D, which is acceptable (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the grade of the background clean area
background area of the closed system or isolator

items.why: no_more: The unit only permits grade D as an acceptable background (a minimum), but 'verify that the background clean area is of grade D' turns that permission into a restriction to exactly grade D.

clauses.text: 9.41. • Production in a closed system, in an isolator, or positive pressure isolators: a background clean area of grade D is acceptable.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Where a cleanroom of a grade lower than B has been considered as the background, is isolator technology used there (recommended)?
items.verify: Where cleanrooms of lower grade than grade B are considered (as the background cleanroom for grade A), verify that isolator technology is used (see paragraph 4.20); such cleanrooms can be considered in that case (recommended).

evidence.what: isolator and the grade of its background cleanroom
layout showing cleanroom grades

items.why: no_more: The unit only permits lower-grade cleanrooms ('can be considered where isolator technology is used'); 'verify that isolator technology is used' turns that permission into a restriction or check.

clauses.text: Cleanrooms of lower grade than grade B can be considered where isolator technology is used (see paragraph 4.20 ).

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Does the filtration system keep fibre and particle generation to a minimum, without unacceptable impurity levels or other change to product quality and efficacy (recommended)?
items.verify: Verify that the filtration system minimizes the generation of fibres and particles, does not cause or contribute to unacceptable levels of impurities, and does not possess characteristics that otherwise alter the quality and efficacy of the product (recommended).

evidence.what: data on fibres, particles and impurities from the filtration system

items.why: code: A8 question drops the qualifier '\bminimi[sz]'

clauses.text: The filtration system should minimize the generation of fibres and particles, not cause or contribute to unacceptable levels of impurities, or possess characteristics that otherwise alter the quality and efficacy of the product.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Where closed and automated systems are used, are they in a grade C environment (usually a hot-cell)?
items.verify: Verify that, in case of use of closed and automated systems (chemical synthesis, purification, on-line sterile filtration), they are in a grade C environment (usually "Hot-cell"), which is the suitable environment.

evidence.what: documents showing the grade of the environment of closed and automated systems
environment of closed and automated systems

items.why: no_more: The unit only says a grade C environment 'will be suitable'; asking 'are they in a grade C environment' turns this suitability statement into a mandatory placement duty.

clauses.text: In case of use of closed and automated systems (chemical synthesis, purification, on-line sterile filtration) a grade C environment (usually “Hot-cell”) will be suitable.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

items.question: Where the expiration dating requirements are not applied to a human OTC drug product under the pending exemption, is its labeling free of dosage limitations and do appropriate stability data support stability of at least 3 years (recommended)?
items.verify: Where a human OTC drug product relies on the requirements in this section not being enforced pending consideration of the proposed exemption published in the Federal Register of September 29, 1978, verify that its labeling does not bear dosage limitations and that it is stable for at least 3 years as supported by appropriate stability data (recommended).

evidence.what: labeling of the human OTC drug product
stability data for the product

items.why: code: A11 (recommended) on must-only units; no_more: The point adds "(recommended)", which weakens a firm condition: the exemption applies only if the labeling has no dosage limitations and the product is stable for at least 3 years. Without these, expiration dating under the section is required.

clauses.text: Pending consideration of a proposed exemption, published in the Federal Register of September 29, 1978, the requirements in this section shall not be enforced for human OTC drug products if their labeling does not bear dosage limitations and they are stable for at least 3 years as supported by appropriate stability data.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov

environmental and process monitoring programme

items.why: code: A8 question drops the qualifier '\bminimi[sz]'

clauses.text: The site’s environmental and process monitoring programme forms part of the overall CCS and is used to monitor the controls designed to minimize the risk of microbial and particle contamination.

items.question: Is the validation documented in line with Annex 15 (recommended), and has the manufacturer identified the process steps that protect subject safety and the trial data?
items.verify: Verify that the validation is documented in accordance with the requirements detailed in EudraLex, Volume 4, Annex 15 (recommended). Verify that, as Article 9(3) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2017/1569 also states, the manufacturer has identified the process steps that safeguard the safety of the subject and the reliability and robustness of the clinical trial data generated in the clinical study.

evidence.what: validation documentation
identified process steps safeguarding subject safety and trial data

items.why: code: A2 must-point marked (recommended)

clauses.text: It should be documented in accordance with the requirements detailed in EudraLex, Volume 4, Annex 15. Article 9(3) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2017/1569 states also that the manufacturer shall identify the process steps that safeguard the safety of the subject and the reliability and robustness of the clinical trial data generated in the clinical study.

items.resolved: shown as other requirement (clause text), owner/lead 20 Nov
